name: Swans
label: Homestead
lede: A New York band that began by making the room hurt, learned to sing, ended itself in 1997, and came back in 2010 with double albums that run two hours.

eras.title: Loud enough to hurt
eras.text: Michael Gira, a demolition worker with a bass, starts a band in a New York that is falling apart, and aims it at the room. The first record he makes with it is called Filth.

years.h: Michael Gira starts Swans with Jonathan Kane on drums
years.p: Gira sings and plays bass, Kane drums, and a rotating cast fills out the rest: Sue Hanel on guitar, Mojo on tape loops, and second bass from Thurston Moore, Dan Braun or Jon Tessler.
years.xp:
Gira had moved to New York in 1979 and played in a band called Circus Mort before Swans. He paid rent doing construction work, including demolition, sheetrock and plastering, according to Wikipedia.

Kane later called Hanel "the most fearsome guitarist we'd ever heard in New York." She was gone before the band recorded, replaced by Bob Pezzola, and saxophonist Daniel Galli-Duani joined.

years.h: Swans EP on Labor: blues chords and awkward time
years.p: The debut EP is no wave with jazz instruments and time signatures that don't sit still, made by the Gira, Kane, Pezzola and Galli-Duani lineup.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the record as minimal chord structures rooted in blues, with jazz instrumentation. Only Gira and Kane survive to the next record.

years.h: Filth: recorded in the Vanguard studio, released on Neutral
years.p: Norman Westberg arrives on guitar and Roli Mosimann on drums for the record where the band stops being a no wave curiosity and becomes a weight.
years.xp:
The sessions were in April 1983 at the Vanguard Records studio in New York. Gira sustained himself on construction work while the city was in what Wikipedia calls severe urban decay.

His goal, in his words: "I wanted the music to obliterate." Robert Christgau's verdict: "Not only isn't it for everybody, it isn't for hardly nobody. I think it's a hoot."

years.h: The early shows: police, and Gira going after headbangers
years.p: According to Wikipedia, the early sets were painfully loud, sometimes drew the police, and Gira stepped on fingers, pulled hair and hit headbangers he disliked.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account says the confrontations with audiences fed into Gira's 1997 decision to end the band.

eras.title: Slower, heavier, and a new voice
eras.text: Two records recorded across an ocean, then the singer who changes what Swans can do walks into rehearsal.

years.h: Cop: Vanguard in New York, Platinum in Zurich
years.p: Gira, Westberg, bassist Harry Crosby and Mosimann slow the tempos down and add tape loops, and end up at number 12 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Recording ran February to May 1984. AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it "quite possibly one of the darkest recordings ever done". Wikipedia lists Godflesh, the Young Gods and Neurosis among the bands it shaped, and Terrorizer ranked it fourth on a 2011 list of the heaviest albums ever.

years.src: Wikipedia: Cop (album) · Wikipedia: Swans (band) · Discogs: Swans, Young God
years.h: Homestead puts out the Young God EP in the US
years.p: The EP shares its title with the band's 1984 British release and gives Gira's later label its name; the 1985 US pressing is on Homestead, according to Discogs.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes the EP was released alongside Cop and is known by its A-sides, "I Crawled" and one with a title that is not repeated here. Gira's voice gets slightly more melodic, still with the snarl.

years.h: Jarboe joins after hearing Filth
years.p: She got hooked on the record, contacted Gira, attended rehearsals and auditioned more than once before he took her on.
years.xp:
She is credited as "scream" on the Time Is Money (Bastard) 12-inch. Bassist Algis Kizys joins in the same period.

Gira coached her singing, she told an interviewer: drop your consonants, and "sing like an American."

eras.title: Jarboe, Cornwall and a major label
eras.text: Swans put down the hammer, pick up piano and oboe, record a Joy Division cover that college radio adopts, and take a shot at MCA.

years.h: Greed: drum machines, grand piano, Jarboe's first record
years.p: K.422 releases it in the UK and PVC in the US, and it reaches number 6 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Recorded June to August 1985 at Intergalactic Studios in New York. The New York Times heard "hammer-on-anvil chording" and chanting voices "like some sinister religious ritual".

years.h: Holy Money: Jarboe sings "You Need Me" and "A Hanging"
years.p: Recorded in the same sessions as Greed and the A Screw single, and it also reached number 6 on the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes Tool's Maynard James Keenan has cited it as a major influence.

years.src: Wikipedia: Public Castration Is a Good Idea
years.h: Public Castration Is a Good Idea, a live album, is taped in London and Nottingham
years.p: Recorded at the ICA and ULU in London and The Garage in Nottingham, it comes out as a semi-official bootleg on Some Bizzare, with a video called A Long Slow Screw.
years.xp: The lineup was Gira, Westberg, Kizys, Jarboe, Ronaldo Gonzalez and drummer Ted Parsons. Thirsty Ear reissued it on CD in 1999.

years.h: Children of God: flute, oboe and cello arrive
years.p: Recorded over six weeks at Sawmills Studios in Cornwall, with Jarboe now a full counterweight to Gira.
years.xp:
Gira's explanation for the turn: "By 1986/7 Swans had run its course with the physical assault of sound." Wikipedia says he feared the band would become cartoonish if it kept going that way.

Caroline released it in the US and K.422 in the UK. Guests included oboist Lindsay Cooper, cellist Audrey Riley and flautist Simon Fraser.

years.h: Gira and Jarboe record two albums as Skin and World of Skin
years.p: Blood, Women, Roses has Jarboe singing lead and Shame, Humility, Revenge has Gira, both slow, sparse and stripped down.
years.xp: The project is called Skin in Europe and World of Skin in the US, according to Wikipedia. A third album, Ten Songs for Another World, follows in 1990.

years.big: "At last, I can make a living"
q: At last, I can make a living at what I love to do.
years.h: Swans cover Joy Division, and MCA calls
years.p: The Love Will Tear Us Apart single, sung by Gira on one version and Jarboe on another, becomes a US college radio hit and an offer from Uni/MCA.
years.xp: Gira, per Wikipedia: he had never seen any money from any of the band's records, and the label offer felt like the payoff for years of work.

years.h: The Burning World: Bill Laswell produces Swans' one major-label album
years.p: Session players and folk textures replace the heavy guitar, and "Saved" reaches number 28 on the US alternative chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports it sold only around 5,000 copies in the UK and was quickly deleted from MCA's catalog. Gira later called the pairing with Laswell a mismatch, while admiring Laswell's wider work. The album includes a cover of Steve Winwood's "Can't Find My Way Home".

eras.title: Their own label, their last albums
eras.text: Back on independent footing, Gira starts Young God Records and makes the run of records that ends with the two-disc Soundtracks for the Blind.

years.h: Gira founds Young God Records, named after the Swans EP
years.p: It starts as an outlet for Swans and later releases Angels of Light, Devendra Banhart, Akron/Family and Larkin Grimm, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: White Light from the Mouth of Infinity
years.h: White Light from the Mouth of Infinity, recorded in New York
years.p: Self-produced, with Jarboe, guitarists Christoph Hahn and Nicky Skopelitis, and drummer Anton Fier.
years.xp: Recorded September 1990 to February 1991 at B. Monster. Wikipedia and Allmusic call it the start of the second half of the band's career.

years.h: Love of Life, recorded by Martin Bisi
years.p: The one Swans album of this period without Norman Westberg, released with the Amnesia EP.

years.h: The Great Annihilator: melody up front, and a Nilsen song
years.p: Recorded across New York and Chicago from February 1993 to June 1994, with a companion Gira solo album, Drainland.
years.xp: Jarboe co-composed two tracks. "Killing for Company" was inspired by the crimes of Dennis Nilsen, per Wikipedia. AllMusic called it an epic; Trouser Press thought the band was running out of ideas.

years.h: Soundtracks for the Blind: 26 tracks and 141 minutes
years.p: Gira built it from cassettes, surveillance tapes and multitrack sessions dating back to 1981, so a 1981 sound plays over one from 1985.
years.xp:
The title comes from recorded conversations with his blind father. Jarboe contributed surveillance tapes her FBI-agent father made of her childhood and her mother's dementia.

AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it "Swans' best album ever". Wikipedia gives the release date as October 29; the discography page says October 22.

years.src: Wikipedia: Swans (band) · Wikipedia: Swans Are Dead
years.h: The farewell tour ends, and Swans stop
years.p: Gira decides to end the band with one last studio album and a world tour, with other projects taking his time.
years.xp: The March 13 Amsterdam Paradiso show is the main source for the live album Swans Are Dead.

eras.title: Angels of Light
eras.text: Gira keeps the label and the songs and drops the volume. Swans exist only as a live album and a memory.

years.h: Swans Are Dead collects two Amsterdam nights
years.p: Disc one is mostly March 1997 at the Paradiso; disc two is the same room in August 1995.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes the 1995 disc was recorded with help from Dutch radio station VPRO.

years.h: Gira starts Angels of Light with New Mother
years.p: A quieter, acoustic-based band, with a rotating cast that later included Kid Congo Powers, Kristof Hahn, Thor Harris and Phil Puleo.
years.xp: Angels of Light ran until 2009 and made albums including How I Loved You and We Are Him. Akron/Family became Gira's backing band and shared a split record with him in 2005.

eras.title: Swans are not dead
eras.text: An Angels of Light show convinces Gira to bring the band back, and the result is a run of double albums that run about two hours.

years.cap: Michael Gira of Swans @ Stylus, Leeds University 5/4/2013 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Swans (band) · Wikipedia: My Father Will Guide Me up a Rope to the Sky
years.h: "SWANS ARE NOT DEAD" appears on MySpace
years.p: Gira posts a new song on the Young God MySpace, and a comeback that no one saw coming is under way.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Gira decided to bring the band back after remembering how elevating and intense the experience was during an Angels of Light performance.

The touring lineup was Gira, Kristof Hahn, Phil Puleo, Norman Westberg, Thor Harris and Christopher Pravdica.

years.src: Wikipedia: My Father Will Guide Me up a Rope to the Sky
years.h: My Father Will Guide Me up a Rope to the Sky pays for itself
years.p: Gira raised money for the sessions by hand-making 1,000 copies of a solo album of demos, I Am Not Insane.
years.xp: Recorded in New York in 12-hour days, and the first Swans album without Jarboe since Greed. It scored 83 on Metacritic.

years.h: The Seer: 119 minutes, and a 32-minute title track
years.p: Karen O sings on "Song for a Warrior"; Jarboe returns on backing vocals; Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker of Low sing on "Lunacy".
years.xp: Funded by the live double album We Rose from Your Bed with the Sun in Our Head and by personalized songs recorded for $500 donors. Gira called it "the culmination of every previous Swans album". Pitchfork gave it 9.0.

years.h: To Be Kind is Swans' highest-charting album
years.p: It reaches number 37 on the US Billboard 200 and 38 in the UK, and runs 121 minutes.
years.xp: Recorded at Sonic Ranch in Texas with producer John Congleton, with St. Vincent and Cold Specks as guests. Bill Rieflin is credited as "Honorary Swan Forever". Pitchfork scored it 9.2.

years.src: Pitchfork: Swans' Michael Gira Issues Statement · Wikipedia: Michael Gira
years.h: Larkin Grimm accuses Michael Gira; he denies the rape charge
years.p: Grimm alleges Gira raped her in 2008; Gira said the encounter was "an awkward mistake" and the accusation "a slanderous lie", per Pitchfork.
years.xp: Grimm, who had been on Gira's Young God label, said she never consented and that a no-sex agreement was part of her contract. Pitchfork's February 26, 2016 story carried Gira's statement and Grimm's reply.

years.h: The Glowing Man closes the trilogy
years.p: 118 minutes across two discs, recorded in seven places from Texas to Berlin, with Bill Rieflin credited as "Hitman and 7th Swan".
years.xp: Wikipedia says the album completes a three-part run with The Seer and To Be Kind, and that "The World Looks Red/The World Looks Black" reuses Gira's words from a 1983 Sonic Youth song with new music.

years.h: The 2010 lineup plays its last shows
years.p: Wikipedia calls The Glowing Man the final album by a mostly stable lineup, after which Gira works with a revolving cast.

eras.title: A revolving cast
eras.text: Gira keeps the name, changes the people, and keeps releasing two-hour records funded by companion albums.

years.h: Leaving Meaning: recorded in Berlin, Reykjavik, Albuquerque and Brooklyn
years.p: Baby Dee sings on "The Nub", and the Necks and Anna von Hausswolff contribute; Larry Mullins and Dana Schechter join the lineup.
years.xp: A March 2019 companion album, What Is This?, financed it. Pitchfork scored it 7.7.

years.h: Bill Rieflin dies at 59
years.p: The drummer who played on Swans records for two decades died of complications from stage 4 colon cancer, diagnosed in 2011, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The Beggar: written in lockdown, funded by Is There Really a Mind?
years.p: Recorded May to August 2022 at Candy Bomber in Berlin, with a 121-minute CD cut and Ben Frost as a guest.
years.xp: Gira says he decided to make Swans "a more open-ended venture, with musicians coming and going from project to project". Released on Mute and Young God.

years.h: Roli Mosimann dies at 68
years.p: The drummer on Filth and Cop died of lung cancer in Wroclaw, Poland, according to Wikipedia; he later produced for the Young Gods and others.

years.h: Birthing: Gira calls it the last "big sound" Swans album
years.p: Material built over a year on the road, then reworked in the studio; future records, he says, will be "significantly pared down".
years.xp: The lead single "I Am a Tower" runs 19 minutes. Metacritic scores it 87.
